title: Document hardware tuning profiles: usage, expected behavior, and troubleshooting
author: Elliot Price
description:
This PR adds internal (public-ish) documentation pages for the Hardware Tuning Profiles pack (H100/B200/L40S) covering: what profiles are, how profile selection works, what “expected behavior” means, safe operating envelopes, common failure modes, and oncall/operator troubleshooting steps. Motivation: we have multiple workstreams landing schema/loader/presets and perf-canary gates; docs need to ship alongside so SRE/CS/field and customers on Private have a single reference for (a) how to reason about profile-enabled rollouts and (b) how to safely override / rollback when something looks off.

Key goals in this doc set: (1) Be explicit about scope: “expected behavior” is guidance based on benchmark methodology, not a contractual guarantee. (2) Make selection + override order legible (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). (3) Provide troubleshooting playbooks (tail latency regression, OOM/fragmentation on L40S, ambiguous GPU SKU detection, multi-GPU/MIG notes) with concrete toggles and what to check in dashboards/logs. (4) Link out to the authoritative artifacts (ADR, schema doc, workload matrix, perf-canary gates, known issues).

What’s included:
- Overview page: Why profiles exist, what changes when enabled, and how we roll them out safely.
- Profile selection + override order: runtime auto-detection, compatibility checks, and precedence rules; how to confirm the selected profile.
- “Expected behavior” pages per SKU (H100/L40S/B200): workload assumptions, throughput vs tail-latency tradeoffs, and when NOT to use the tuned mode.
- Troubleshooting guide: symptom -> likely cause -> verification steps -> mitigations/rollback.
- FAQ for Support/Solutions: what’s safe to change, what requires Eng involvement, and how to collect a minimal triage bundle.

Not included:
- Any changes to runtime behavior itself (this is docs-only), and no new external/marketing site content. This is intended for internal docs + Private operator reference.

Rollout note: this will be linked from the runtime release notes and from the rollout runbook. Wording has been reviewed to avoid overpromising; we consistently use “expected behavior”, “typical”, and “observed in benchmark suite” with explicit workload envelopes and caveats.

notable_snippets: Terminology block added across pages: “expected behavior” = observed in benchmark suite; not a guarantee; depends on workload envelope (seq length distro, concurrency, streaming/tool-calling mix) and runtime version compatibility.

Troubleshooting snippet: “If p95 increases >X% while tokens/sec improves, first verify prefill/decode fairness settings and check streaming tail for queue backpressure; mitigation is to switch to balanced mode or disable profile at pool level per runbook.”

Private operator snippet: “Overrides must be applied via Helm values in supported keys only; avoid partial overrides of internal kernel toggles unless directed by Runtime Eng; always attach effective config dump + startup compatibility log line in support requests.”
review_conversation: Kira Thompson: Troubleshooting section is strong. Please add a single “Oncall quick start” at the top with 5 steps max and links to the detailed sections. Also add explicit rollback criteria language and where to record the decision.

Elliot Price (author): Added “Oncall quick start” block + a rollback criteria callout; linked to rollout runbook and incident template. Also added a note: capture pool/region, selected profile metric, and effective config dump before rollback to help root-cause.
Neha Kapoor: Wording needs to be careful: don’t imply SLO guarantees. Replace “will improve” with “typically improves” and add a disclaimer that perf varies by workload and capacity conditions.

Elliot Price (author): Updated language across all expected behavior pages; added a consistent disclaimer section and changed headings from “Performance improvements” to “Typical deltas (benchmark suite)”.

Claire Dubois: In the workload envelope sections, please name the workload matrix dimensions we actually test (seq buckets, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming). Also link the methodology page rather than paraphrasing too much.
Elliot Price (author): Added explicit bullets for seq length buckets + concurrency levels, and added a single canonical link for methodology/workload matrix to reduce drift.

Hiro Tanaka: H100 page: add a “when not to use throughput-first mode” example (short prompts + high request rate can hurt streaming p95). Also call out that kernel selection is seq-len bucketed and that anomalies should be validated against bucket distribution.
Elliot Price (author): Added the example and a “validate your bucket mix” section with suggested metrics to check (prompt tokens histogram, decode length histogram, streaming duration).

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler section should mention fairness/backpressure knobs at a conceptual level but avoid listing every internal knob name (those are in schema docs and change). Suggest: describe modes and observable symptoms, and link to schema reference for exact keys.
Elliot Price (author): Reworked scheduler section to be mode-oriented; removed unstable key names; added link to schema reference and updated troubleshooting mapping to symptoms rather than knobs.
Marissa Cole: Add a short section on customer-facing communication: how Support should describe changes when a customer sees different latency after a rollout.
Elliot Price (author): Added “Support comms guidance” in FAQ with approved phrasing and escalation triggers (include p95 delta threshold, error rate changes, OOM/retry spikes).
Paula Mendes: Please add a note in the perf-canary linkage about noise/flakiness and that only gated metrics should block rollouts; others are “investigate”.
Elliot Price (author): Added a “Gates vs signals” callout and consistent wording: gates block promotion; signals create a ticket for investigation.
release_notes: Internal docs: Added Hardware Tuning Profiles documentation (usage, selection/overrides, per-SKU expected behavior, troubleshooting + oncall quick start). Linked from runtime rollout guidance to reduce misconfiguration and speed up triage.
